subject.title: autoreview: secret-scanner false positives on identifier and member-expression values (e.g. `apiSecret: ctx.cloudinary.apiSecret`)

question: Should autoreview accept all parser-verified JavaScript/TypeScript identifier and member-expression credential references, or retain a curated source-root allowlist?
rationale: Both approaches can reduce false positives, but they establish different fail-closed boundaries for a tool that intentionally prevents secret material from entering review bundles.

options.title: Use syntactic reference validation
options.body: Accept only parser-verified pure identifier/member expressions in JavaScript and TypeScript, while retaining all literal and token detectors.

options.title: Expand the vetted allowlist
options.body: Keep the current root-based policy and add only specifically approved runtime roots such as provider configuration objects.

options.title: Add an explicit escape hatch
options.body: Keep detection strict by default but offer a documented redaction or override path for verified false positives.

recommendation.title: Use syntactic reference validation
recommendation.body: Accept only parser-verified pure identifier/member expressions in JavaScript and TypeScript, while retaining all literal and token detectors.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the merged source-reference verifier whose policy boundary this decision extends.
